plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the operation of the BUILD-MAX-HEAP procedure on a 10-element input array A = ⟨4, 1, 3, 2, 16, 9, 10, 14, 8, 7⟩ across six panels (a)–(f). At the top of the figure, the input array A is displayed as a horizontal row of ten labeled cells. Each panel shows the heap as a rooted binary tree in which every node is labeled with its array index (small numeral outside the circle) and its current key value (numeral inside the circle); light gray nodes are unmodified and the single dark gray node labeled i marks the root of the subtree currently being processed by MAX-HEAPIFY. Panel (a) shows the initial tree before any heapification, with i = 5 (value 16) — the first call to MAX-HEAPIFY starting from index ⌊n/2⌋ = 5. Panel (b) shows the state with i = 4 (value 2), after MAX-HEAPIFY has been applied at index 5. Panel (c) shows i = 3 (value 3), with the subtree at index 4 already corrected to place 14 above 2 and 8. Panel (d) shows i = 2 (value 1). Panel (e) shows i = 1 (value 4), the final call, where the root must be sifted down. Panel (f) shows the completed max-heap with root 16, in which no dark node appears and every parent holds a value greater than or equal to its children. This figure illustrates how BUILD-MAX-HEAP constructs a max-heap in place by calling MAX-HEAPIFY on each internal node from index ⌊n/2⌋ down to index 1.

elements: array bar: horizontal row of 10 cells labeled A, values 4, 1, 3, 2, 16, 9, 10, 14, 8, 7 with index ticks 1–10
binary tree of 10 circular nodes, each showing key value inside and array index as a small numeral beside the circle
edges connecting each node to its left child (2i) and right child (2i+1)
dark gray shaded node marking the current index i being heapified
comparison arrows from node i to its children during sift-down
legend / status line showing current call MAX-HEAPIFY(A, i) and which lines execute
final panel state: completed max-heap with root 16 and no shaded node

interactions.label: Implement MAX-HEAPIFY

api.does: highlights nodes i and j and draws comparison arrows; returns true when value(i) > value(j)
exchange the keys at indices i and j — the ONLY way to mutate the heap
shade node i dark gray as the current sift position

interactions.frame: the array bar and the full 10-node tree, with the current node i shaded dark gray, comparison arrows to its children, and the just-swapped pair flashing
interactions.success_check: every parent holds a value greater than or equal to both of its children (root ends as 16)
interactions.teaches: MAX-HEAPIFY only fixes one violation at a time and must recurse into the child it swapped with — without the recursive call the subtree below can remain broken, which the replay makes visible

demo_steps.title: The input as a tree
demo_steps.narration: The array A = ⟨4,1,3,2,16,9,10,14,8,7⟩ is laid out as a complete binary tree: index labels sit beside each circle, key values inside. Leaves (indices 6–10) are already trivially heaps, so work starts at ⌊n/2⌋ = 5.

demo_steps.title: Write MAX-HEAPIFY
demo_steps.narration: Implement maxHeapify(i, heapSize): find the largest among node i and its two children, swap if needed, then recurse into the child you swapped with. Run it and watch the dark gray node i sift down with comparison arrows at each step.

demo_steps.title: Run BUILD-MAX-HEAP
demo_steps.narration: The driver calls your maxHeapify for i = 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 — reproducing panels (a) through (e). Because children are processed before parents, each call can assume its subtrees are already valid heaps.

demo_steps.title: Verify the max-heap
demo_steps.narration: The final tree (panel f) has 16 at the root and every parent ≥ its children. Try the buggy version without the recursive call and watch where the heap property silently fails.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: BUILD-MAX-HEAP works bottom-up from index ⌊n/2⌋ to 1 precisely so that each MAX-HEAPIFY call can assume both subtrees are already heaps — and MAX-HEAPIFY must recurse after a swap, or the violation just moves down one level.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Two linked views: the 10-cell array bar on top (cells labeled with index numbers 1–10 above, values inside) and the complete binary tree below it with the standard heap layout (root 4 at top, children 1 and 3, etc.). Nodes are light gray circles with the array index as a small numeral just outside the upper-left of each circle and the key value large inside. During replay the active node i is filled dark gray and labeled 'i', matching the textbook shading; comparison arrows point from i to whichever children are examined. The tree shape and index positions never change — only the key values inside the circles swap, exactly as in panels (a)–(f). Final state must match panel (f): root 16, left subtree rooted at 14 (children 8, 7), right subtree rooted at 10 (children 9, 3).

discrepancies: The default state shows no dark-gray marked node with the italic 'i' label, whereas every source panel (a)-(e) prominently marks the current sift position i — the 'i' marker only appears after running the simulation
Index labels (1-10) beside nodes and the array are rendered very small (~9-10px) compared with the clearly legible small numerals in the source, hurting readability at inline size

The source's six side-by-side panels (a)-(f) showing successive heap states are replaced by a single animated tree, so the static multi-snapshot comparison the textbook figure provides is only accessible via playback

Node fill in the source is a two-tone scheme (light gray normal, dark gray for i); the generated figure adds orange/red highlight fills for swaps/comparisons/violations that don't exist in the source (acceptable pedagogically but changes the look)
evaluation.notes: The tree topology, array bar, and BUILD-MAX-HEAP semantics faithfully reproduce CLRS Figure 6.2, and the editable-code workbench with frame playback and a buggy-variant demo is pedagogically excellent; the main weaknesses are the absent 'i' marker in the default view and the very small index labels versus the source's legible annotations.
action_items: Show the marked node (dark fill with italic 'i' at index 5, value 16) in the default initial frame so the drop-in state matches panel (a) of the source instead of an unmarked tree
Increase the index-number font size (both beside tree nodes and above the array cells) so the 1-10 indices are comfortably readable at inline size
Add visible (a)-(f)-style captions or a frame indicator tied to the five MAX-HEAPIFY calls so users can map playback frames back to the textbook panels

feedback.rationale: The concept and topology are faithful (concept_accuracy 5, faithfulness 4), but concrete execution fixes remain — showing the marked 'i' node in the default frame, enlarging index-label fonts, and adding panel-style frame indicators — all implementation-level issues the generator can address without changing the plan.
